newsitem.title: USA: Four Corners 750 MW coal-fired unit seen up Sat.
newsitem.headline: Four Corners 750 MW coal-fired unit seen up Sat.

text.p: The 750 megawatt (MW) unit 5 at the Four Corners coal-fired power plant in New Mexico is scheduled to be back on-line early Saturday morning, sources familiar with the plant's operations said Tuesday.
The unit has been shut for unplanned repair work since early last Tuesday.
Meanwhile, Four Corner's 750 MW unit 4 was back to full power after restarting late Monday, the sources said.
Unit 4 operated at a curtailed rate last week and was shut over the weekend for mechanical repairs.
Four Corner's units 1, 2 and 3 were said to be operating near normal rates of 167 MW, 170 MW and 220 MW, respectively.
Arizona Public Service Co operates Four Corners and owns units 1, 2 and 3 along with 15 percent of units 4 and 5.
Southern California Edison Co holds a 48 percent stake in units 4 and 5.
